diagnostic_evidence.quote: Indeed, suppose that a linear encoder $\Psi'$ is injective on a linear subspace $V \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ with $\text{dim}(V)=n$.
It is always possible to decompose $f(p)$ into a contribution in $V$ and one in its orthogonal complement, i.e. $f(p) = f_V(p) + f_{V^\perp}(p)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The step F(p) = J_Psi' f_V(p) silently assumes J_Psi' f_Vperp(p) = 0, i.e. ker(J_Psi') = V^perp. The hypotheses give only V ∩ ker(J_Psi') = {0} (injectivity on V), which does not force the kernel to be the orthogonal complement of V. Hence the conclusion 'invertibility of F requires that f_V is invertible' is false. Counterexample: N=2, n=1, J_Psi' = [1,1], V = span(e1), f(p) = (phi(p), p - phi(p)) with phi even and non-injective (e.g. phi(p)=p^2 on (-1,1)): f is injective, F(p) = J_Psi' f(p) = p is invertible (so the linear encoder is injective on M), yet f_V(p) = (phi(p),0) is not invertible and J_Psi' f_V(p) = p^2 ≠ p = F(p).

failure_location.quote: Then $F(p) = J_{\Psi'}f_V(p)$, and invertibility of $F$ requires that $f_V(p)$ is invertible.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the encoder realizes the orthogonal projection onto V (i.e. ker(J_Psi') = V^perp), or replace V by the row space of J_Psi' and re-derive; the proposition's message then holds.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed parameterization of M by coordinates on the presupposed subspace V is unreliable, and the derivation supporting the linear-encoder analysis (including th:linear_nonlinear, which is presented as a consequence of this proposition) is unsound as written.
issues.title: Linear-encoder proposition: invalid decomposition step and false invertibility conclusion
issues.why_classification: The headline claim (linear encoders are injective exactly on manifolds parameterizable via a linear subspace) is true and survives; only the local derivation and the identification of the correct subspace need routine correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A linear--non-linear autoencoder can reproduce with null representation error manifolds described by $f = f_V + f_{V^\perp}$, where $f_{V^\perp} \perp f_V$ (\textbf{\Cref{th:linear_nonlinear}}).
It is always possible to decompose $f(p)$ into a contribution in $V$ and one in its orthogonal complement, i.e. $f(p) = f_V(p) + f_{V^\perp}(p)$.
In the following examples, we choose $f_V$ to be a linear map and thus consider manifolds of the form $x_N = Ax_n + g(x_n)$, with $A \in \mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ full rank and $g(x_n) \perp Ax_n$.

issues.failure_explanation: Every parameterization f admits the orthogonal decomposition f = f_V + f_Vperp (the orthogonality is automatic by construction), so the stated hypothesis does not restrict the manifold class at all. As written the proposition therefore asserts that a linear encoder with nonlinear decoder reproduces every manifold with null representation error, which is false: e.g. the circle S^1 in R^2 with n=1 admits no linear map from R^2 to R injective on it (any linear functional is constant on chords parallel to its kernel). The needed hypothesis - invertibility of f_V, i.e. M is a graph over V, which the paper's own examples impose by taking f_V linear of full rank - is missing from the statement.

failure_location.quote: (A linear--non-linear autoencoder can reproduce with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ manifolds described by $f = f_V + f_{V^\perp}$)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypothesis that f_V is invertible (the manifold is a graph over V), matching the examples in the same section; the characterization is then correct.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition, restated among the paper's main results, overstates the class of manifolds exactly representable with a linear encoder; the correct class (graphs over a linear subspace) is strictly smaller.
issues.title: Linear-non-linear autoencoder proposition has a vacuous hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The literal claim is false, and the repair necessarily narrows the advertised class from all manifolds to graph manifolds - a limited weakening that leaves a recognizable but strictly weaker characterization.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This theorem leads to the following proposition about fully non-linear autoencoders.
there is a ReLU neural network $N_f$ with input dimension $n_{\text{in}}$, hidden layer widths at most $w$, and output dimension $n_{\text{out}}$ that $\varepsilon$-approximates $f$
We call $n$ the latent size, $\Psi':\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}^n$, $m\leq n<N$, the encoder

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition is stated with no proof, and its invoked support (the universal approximation theorem, th:uap) cannot establish it: UAT provides epsilon-approximation with growing networks - an approximation-error (Varepsilon_2) statement in the paper's own error taxonomy - whereas Varepsilon_1 = 0 requires exact reproduction of the identity on M by an architecture, an exact-representation and injectivity statement UAT says nothing about. Under the standing assumption m <= n < N the claim is even false for n = m: no compact m-manifold embeds in R^m (invariance of domain), e.g. a circle cannot be encoded in R^1. No relation between n and m (such as n >= 2m+1), no manifold class, and no activation assumptions are specified.

failure_location.quote: A non-linear--non-linear autoencoder can reproduce with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ generic manifolds

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State a precise version with explicit hypotheses (compact m-manifold, n >= 2m+1 via an embedding theorem, specified activations) and supply the missing construction showing that a network of the proposed architecture realizes an injective encoder with exact inverse on M; nothing in the source currently establishes the claim.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claim that fully non-linear autoencoders achieve null representation error on generic manifolds is unsupported; the architectural guidance that follows rests on th:reduction, which is itself defective.
issues.title: Unproven claim that non-linear autoencoders exactly represent generic manifolds
issues.why_classification: Repairing requires a contained but genuinely new construction (embedding plus network realizability) or a substantive weakening to a provable statement; the claim as written is neither proved by the cited results nor true for n = m.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: y^{(\ell)} = \sigma^{(\ell)}\left(W^{(\ell)} y^{(\ell-1)} + b^{(\ell)}\right).

To ensure the injectivity of the encoder approximated by a neural network, each layer must be injective, condition which is satisfied when $n_\ell \geq n_{\ell-1}$ for all hidden layers, so $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$ for $\ell = 1,\ldots,L-1$.
By \Cref{th:uap}, we have that $n_\ell = n_\text{in}+n_\text{out}$ is sufficient to satisfy $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ and $\lim_{|\myw|\to\infty}\Varepsilon_2 = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed sufficient condition is false: a layer y = sigma(W y + b) with n_l >= n_{l-1} can be non-injective - any rank-deficient W (e.g. W = 0) makes the layer constant, and a non-injective activation (ReLU, as in the cited th:uap) makes the layer non-injective regardless of width. The proof's inferences are invalid: dimension alone implies neither full column rank nor injective activations, and th:uap is an approximation result that says nothing about injectivity or about Varepsilon_1 = 0. Moreover the final layer phi' from R^M to R^n with M >= N > n cannot be injective on all of R^M; injectivity on the reshaped manifold requires a separate genericity/embedding-dimension argument that is missing.

failure_location.quote: A sufficient condition for the width to ensure injectivity of the encoder is $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$, for $\ell = 1,\ldots, L-1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate with the needed hypotheses: injective activation functions, weight matrices of full column rank (generic for n_l >= n_{l-1}), and a final linear layer injective on the reshaped manifold (available generically for n at least about 2m+1); the design message then survives.
issues.overall_effect: The stated sufficient condition for Varepsilon_1 = 0 - used to justify the design rule of performing dimensionality reduction only at the last encoder layer, and highlighted as a main result - is not established and is false as stated.
issues.title: Width condition does not ensure encoder injectivity; proof is a non sequitur
issues.why_classification: A recognizable version of the theorem survives after adding standard hypotheses and rebuilding the proof (including a genericity argument for the last layer), but the statement as given is false and its proof is invalid.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the map $B_r((t^*, \mu^*)) \ni (t, \mu) \to u_N$ is injective $\forall (t^*, \mu^*) \in [0,T]\times\mathcal{P}$, with $r$ small enough
We conclude that $U$ is locally Euclidean, so $\{u_N(t;\mu)\}_{t\in[0,T], \mu \in \mathcal{P}}$ is a $a$-manifold, that we denote by $\mathcal{M}$.
$U = \{u_N(t;\mu)\}_{B_r((t^*,\mu^*))}$, where $B_r(\cdot)$ is the closed ball of radius $r$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows that each local image U is homeomorphic to a ball in parameter-time space, then concludes the whole set is locally Euclidean. This fails twice. (i) The images U need not be neighborhoods in M: the hypothesis is mere local injectivity of (t,mu) -> u_N, under which trajectories of different parameters can cross transversally (ODE uniqueness only prevents self-crossings within a single trajectory); at a crossing point no neighborhood in M is homeomorphic to an open subset of R^a, so M need not be a manifold at all. (ii) Even under global injectivity, the domain [0,T] x P and the closed balls used have boundaries, so the image is at best a manifold with boundary, not an a-manifold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to global injectivity of (t,mu) -> u_N (as the paper itself obtains via augmentation of the data) and weaken the conclusion to 'M is homeomorphic to [0,T] x P, an a-dimensional compact set (manifold with boundary) of topological dimension a'; th:latent_dim then follows from Menger-Nobeling.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the parametric solution set is an a-manifold - a main result - is unestablished; th:latent_dim, whose proof presupposes that M is a compact space of topological dimension a, inherits the gap.
issues.title: Local injectivity does not imply the solution set is a manifold
issues.why_classification: Both the hypothesis (local to global injectivity) and the conclusion (manifold to manifold with boundary) must be changed, but a recognizably comparable result and the downstream latent-dimension bound survive with a contained repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \underbrace{(M_{J_{\Psi'}}L_{F_N} + M_{F_N}L_{J_{\Psi'}}) L_\Psi}_{= \overline{L}_{F_n,\mu}}
$M_{J_{\Psi'}} \coloneqq \sup_{u_N \in \mathcal{M}} \|J_{\Psi'}(u_N)\|$

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses assume Psi and Psi' Lipschitz, J_Psi' Lipschitz and bounded, and F_N bounded - but never that F_N is Lipschitz. The derived bound nevertheless uses the Lipschitz constant L_{F_N} of F_N (the appendix computation applies the estimate ||F_N(Psi(u_n1)) - F_N(Psi(u_n2))|| <= L_{F_N} ||Psi(u_n1)-Psi(u_n2)||), which is undefined under the stated assumptions. In addition, M_{J_Psi'} and M_{F_N} are suprema over M while the bound is claimed for the Lipschitz constant of F_n on R^n, where Psi(u_n) need not lie in M.

failure_location.quote: Additionally, we assume that $F_N$ is bounded, with $M_{F_N} \coloneqq \sup_{u_N\in\mathcal{M}} \|F_N(u_N)\|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that F_N is Lipschitz (with constant L_{F_N}) on a set containing the range of Psi - or localize the statement to a neighborhood of M - and take the suprema over that set.
issues.overall_effect: The Lipschitz bound for F_n, and with it the well-posedness of the reduced problem (th:well_posedness_node, whose proof cites this proposition), is unestablished as stated.
issues.title: Lipschitz bound for F_n uses unassumed Lipschitz continuity of F_N
issues.why_classification: A routine addition of a standard hypothesis (Lipschitz continuity of F_N and correct scoping of the constants) repairs the proposition and its dependent well-posedness claim with no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Due to the specific assumptions made in the construction of the decoder, the projection sets some eigenvalues to zero while leaving the others unchanged.
We now assume the construction of an autoencoder that realizes an orthogonal projection.
Without additional assumptions, the eigenvalues of $A$ differ from those of $\Lambda$ leading to a different bound on the timestep size with respect to that of the \Node.

issues.failure_explanation: The eigenvalues of the reduced matrix A = J_Psi' Lambda J_Psi are those of the compression of Lambda to the latent subspace S (P = J_Psi J_Psi' the orthogonal projection), and a compression to a subspace that is not Lambda-invariant does not have eigenvalues drawn from the spectrum of Lambda. Counterexample: Lambda = [[-2,1],[1,-2]] (eigenvalues -1,-3) with S = span(e1) gives compression eigenvalue -2, which is not an eigenvalue of Lambda. Worse, with stable Lambda = [[-1,0,100],[0,-2,0],[0,0,-1]] and S = span(e2, e1+e3) (which contains the solution manifold on the e2-axis, so the orthogonal-projection autoencoder is exact on it), the reduced matrix has eigenvalue +49, so no Forward Euler timestep is stable: the claimed 'at worst the same' bound does not exist. Eigenvalue preservation requires S to be Lambda-invariant (e.g. the manifold spanning the latent subspace), an assumption never stated.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, the eigenvalues $\neq 0$ are those of $\Lambda$, so the bound on the timestep of the \node\ is, in the worst scenario, the same as that of the \Node.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypothesis that the latent subspace is Lambda-invariant (equivalently, the reduction is tight, the manifold spanning the decoder range); under it the nonzero eigenvalues of A are eigenvalues of Lambda and the conclusion holds.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee that with an orthogonal-projection decoder the reduced FE stability limit is never worse than the full-order one is unsupported and false within the paper's own framework (e.g. whenever the latent dimension exceeds the dimension of the span of the manifold, as allowed by n up to 2a+1).
issues.title: A-stability: orthogonal projection does not preserve eigenvalues or the timestep bound
issues.why_classification: The derivation is invalid and the conclusion fails without an added invariance hypothesis; with that hypothesis a comparable but narrower guarantee survives - a limited weakening rather than a collapse of the stability analysis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A necessary condition to meet the requirement $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$ is that $\tau_n^k, \zeta_k \to 0$ and $\kappa \to 0$.
Then, setting \eqref{eq:what_nn_learns_1} to zero and comparing it to \eqref{eq:diff_op_tau}, we conclude that
Using the fully data-driven training, by \Cref{th:fully_works}, we have that $\eps_{F_n} \to 0$ as $|\myw| \to \infty$ and $\Delta t_{\text{train}} \to 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition asserts convergence of the fully data-driven training 'under proper conditions', but no such conditions are specified and no sufficiency argument is given: the preceding derivation merely compares the zero-residual identity with the exact difference equation and extracts necessary conditions (tau, zeta -> 0 and kappa -> 0). Necessity does not establish convergence; the comparison in fact shows that the learned right-hand side absorbs stepwise differences of the encoder error kappa and the data error zeta, whose control requires more than uniform vanishing of kappa and zeta (rate/derivative control), so the claimed convergence does not follow from what is argued. The proof of th:global_convergence then rests on this unestablished claim for its final limit statement.

failure_location.quote: The fully data-driven is a convergent method for training $N_{F_n}$ in the sense that, under proper conditions, $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove sufficiency under explicit conditions (control of kappa and zeta at the needed rates, identifiability from the residual equations on sufficiently dense data) or weaken the proposition to the necessary-condition statement actually derived, adjusting the limit claim of th:global_convergence accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence guarantee of the fully data-driven training, and the final limit statement of the global convergence theorem for that training route, are unsupported.
issues.title: Fully data-driven convergence claimed but only necessary conditions established
issues.why_classification: The argument establishes materially less than the statement; repairing requires a genuine convergence analysis or a substantive weakening of the claimed guarantee, both contained within the existing framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: H = \|\m w_n - \m u_n \|_\infty \leq (\eps_{\Psi'} + \eps_{F_n}T) e^{L_{F_n,\mu} T}.

\leq L_{\Psi}\|\m u_n - \m w_n\|_{\infty} + L_{\Psi}\|\m w_n - \m \uut_n\|_{\infty} + \eps_{\Psi} \leq L_{\Psi}(\eps_{\Psi'} + \eps_{F_n}T) e^{L_{F_n,\mu} T} + L_{\Psi}C_{1,\mu}\Delta t^P + \eps_{\Psi}.$

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions require only continuity of Psi', Psi and F_n, yet the stated bound and its proof use Lipschitz constants: Gronwall's lemma is applied via ||F_n(w_n)-F_n(u_n)|| <= L_{F_n}||w_n-u_n||, and the reconstruction step uses ||Psi(u_n)-Psi(w_n)|| <= L_Psi||u_n-w_n||. For merely continuous maps these constants need not exist, so both the bound, as a statement, and its proof are unfounded under the declared hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the assumptions to Lipschitz continuity of Psi and F_n (as informally assumed elsewhere in the paper); the bound and its proof then go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central global error bound is unproven under its stated assumptions.
issues.title: Global convergence theorem assumes continuity but its proof and bound use Lipschitz constants
issues.why_classification: A routine hypothesis upgrade (continuity to Lipschitz) repairs the theorem with no loss of conclusion, rate, or advertised scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To this aim, a simple strategy is to modify the loss function by adding a contribution whose minimization enforces conservation:
$\sum_{k=1}^{N} [u_{N}(t)]_k = \sum_{k=1}^{N} [u_{N0}]_k, \quad \forall t \in [0, T].$

issues.failure_explanation: The stated goal is to enforce conservation of the total concentration, but the defined term is a sum of squared componentwise differences between the reference and reconstructed solutions - a pointwise trajectory-matching penalty. It is insensitive to how reconstruction errors distribute across components: two candidate reconstructions with equal pointwise squared errors but differently signed errors have the same loss but different total-concentration errors (e.g. error vectors (1,-1,0,...) and (sqrt(2),0,0,...) give identical loss but conservation errors 0 and sqrt(2)). Minimizing this term therefore cannot enforce the sum invariant it is claimed to enforce; a conservation-enforcing term must penalize the difference of the sums.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term with a penalty on the conservation violation, e.g. the square of the difference between the summed reference concentrations and the summed reconstructed concentrations at each time step.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed conservation-preserving training strategy for the chemical kinetics test case does not do what is stated; the approximate conservation observed numerically is attributable to reconstruction accuracy, not to this loss term.
issues.title: Proposed conservation loss does not enforce conservation
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the loss formula preserves the intended strategy, the training procedure, and all reported results; only the mis-specified term must be replaced.
